angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 313,761 km at 80.59 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.4085 +/- 0.0185 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 80.59 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.451 +/- 0.085 solar radii from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4479 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract): 313,761 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.452 +/- 0.09 solar masses from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4479 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3400 +/- 100 K from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4479 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4479 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4479.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.785, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4479 (pscomppars): spectral type M3.0, from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, TOI-4479: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4479 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0 dex, from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4479 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.60432, from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
